# Meridian Public Library - Public API Specification v1.3

This document is the complete contract for the Meridian Public Library public HTTP API, version 1.3. Where an example conflicts with a numbered clause, the numbered clause governs.

## A. Purpose and conventions

C-01. This API provides machine-readable access to the library catalog search and to member loan management.

C-02. The base URL is https://api.meridianlib.example/v1; all endpoint paths in this document are relative to it.

C-03. All request and response bodies are JSON encoded as UTF-8 with Content-Type application/json.

C-04. The API major version is part of the path (v1); the minor version is reported in the X-Api-Version response header and is currently 1.3.

C-05. All timestamps are ISO 8601 strings in UTC.

C-06. Every response includes an X-Request-Id header; clients are encouraged to log it for support tickets.

C-07. Terminology: a book is a catalog record; a copy is a physical item; a loan is the checkout of one copy by one member.

## B. Authentication and errors

C-08. Every request must carry an X-Api-Key header containing a valid API key.

C-09. A missing or invalid key is rejected with HTTP 401 and error code invalid_api_key.

C-10. A valid key belonging to a revoked account is rejected with HTTP 403 and error code forbidden.

C-11. A request for a resource that does not exist is rejected with HTTP 404 and error code not_found.

C-12. A request that fails validation is rejected with HTTP 400 and error code validation_error; the message field names the offending parameter.

## C. Pagination and rate limits

C-13. All list endpoints paginate with the query parameters page (1-based) and page_size.

C-14. page_size defaults to 20 and may be set up to a maximum of 100; larger values are rejected with HTTP 400.

C-15. Paginated responses carry page, page_size, total_items, and total_pages.

C-16. A page number beyond total_pages returns an empty items array rather than a 404.

C-17. Clients are limited to 60 requests per minute per API key.

C-18. Exceeding the rate limit yields HTTP 429 with error code rate_limited and a Retry-After header giving the wait in seconds.

C-19. A request body larger than 1 MiB is rejected with HTTP 413 and error code payload_too_large.

## D. Catalog

C-20. GET /books searches the catalog; the q parameter matches against title and author, and the genre parameter filters by genre tag.

C-21. A book record contains id, title, author, isbn13, genre, available, and copies.

C-22. available is true exactly when at least one copy of the book is not currently on loan.

C-23. isbn13 is a string of exactly 13 digits.

C-24. GET /books/{id} returns a single book record, or 404 if the id is unknown.

C-25. Book ids are stable strings prefixed bk-.

C-26. Catalog search results are sorted by title ascending; v1 offers no client-supplied sort parameter.

## E. Loans

C-27. POST /loans with body {book_id, card_number} creates a loan for that book and card.

C-28. POST /loans fails with HTTP 409 and error code no_copy_available when no copy is currently available.

C-29. A loan record contains id, book_id, card_number, checkout_date, due_date, returned_date (nullable), and status.

C-30. Loan status is one of pending, active, returned, cancelled.

C-31. A newly created loan is pending and becomes active when the copy is picked up; pickup handling is out of band for v1.

C-32. The loan period is 21 days: due_date is checkout_date plus 21 days.

C-33. A member may hold at most 5 active loans per card; a sixth POST /loans is rejected with HTTP 409 and error code loan_limit_reached.

C-34. DELETE /loans/{id} cancels a loan; only loans in status pending may be cancelled.

C-35. A cancelled loan has status cancelled; a returned loan has status returned with returned_date stamped.

C-36. Overdue loans accrue a fine of 0.25 USD per day, capped at 10.00 USD per loan.

## F. Holds and renewals

C-37. POST /books/{id}/holds queues a hold for the calling member; holds are served in creation order.

C-38. Once notified that a copy is available, a member has 72 hours to claim it before the hold expires.

C-39. A loan may be renewed at most 2 times; each renewal extends due_date by 21 days.

C-40. A renewal request is refused with HTTP 409 and error code hold_exists when any hold is queued on the book.

## G. Members and limits summary

C-41. Library card numbers are strings of exactly 14 digits.

C-42. GET /members/{card_number} returns the member's active loans and holds.

C-43. Global request limits for v1 are: request body at most 1 MiB; at most 60 requests per minute per key; page_size cap of 250.

C-44. Endpoints or parameters not listed in this document do not exist in v1; undocumented behavior is not supported.

C-45. Changes to this contract are published as new minor versions with a changelog; the present document describes v1.3 only.

# Heron Telemetry Agent - Configuration Schema and Validation Rules v2.1

This document specifies the agent.yaml configuration file for the Heron telemetry agent, version 2.1, and the exact validation behavior of the loader.

## A. Overview

C-01. Heron is a single-binary agent that ingests telemetry events and flushes them to a configured backend.

C-02. All configuration lives in a single YAML file named agent.yaml located in the working directory.

C-03. The loader validates the whole file at startup; a valid config is a precondition for running.

C-04. This document describes schema (which keys exist), constraints (allowed values), and behavior (what the agent does with them).

C-05. Durations are written as integers with an explicit unit suffix in the key name (interval_seconds, backoff_initial_ms).

C-06. Boolean keys accept only true and false.

## B. File format and validation

C-07. The top-level mapping may contain exactly these keys: service, ingest, flush, logging, security, metrics.

C-08. An unknown top-level key is a validation error.

C-09. An unknown key inside a section is also a validation error; per-section allowed keys are listed in their sections below.

C-10. On any validation error the loader prints the offending key path and exits with exit code 2.

C-11. On success the loader exits validation with exit code 0 and the agent starts.

C-12. Validation errors are cumulative: the loader reports every invalid key, not just the first.

C-13. Comments and blank lines are permitted anywhere in the file and never affect validation.

## C. service section

C-14. service.name is required and must be a string of 1 to 63 characters.

C-15. service.environment is one of production, staging, development and defaults to development.

C-16. service.instance_id is optional; when present it must be a non-empty string of at most 128 characters.

C-17. service.name appears in every emitted log line.

## D. ingest section

C-26. retry.max_attempts is the number of flush attempts per cycle, default 3, allowed range 1 to 10.

C-27. retry.backoff_initial_ms is the first retry delay, default 200, and doubles on each subsequent attempt within a cycle.

C-28. The retry delay is capped at 30 seconds regardless of the number of attempts.

C-30. Log lines are single-line JSON with keys ts, level, msg.

C-31. logging.level=debug additionally enables request/response dumps and per-batch counters.

C-32. When logging.level is debug, flush.interval_seconds may be set as low as 2 to speed up local iteration.

C-33. The log level can only be set in agent.yaml, never overridden by environment variables.

C-35. security.tls.mode=disabled is only valid when service.environment is development; in staging or production it is a validation error.

C-36. With security.tls.mode=required, non-TLS connections are refused at handshake.

C-37. security.ca_file is optional and, when present, must point to an existing file; a missing file is a validation error.

C-39. metrics.port is the metrics listen port, default 9102, allowed range 1024 to 65535.

# Driftless File-Sync Service - Behavior Matrix v4.2

This document is the complete behavior specification for the Driftless file-sync client and service, version 4.2. Numbered clauses are normative.

## A. Overview and model

C-01. Driftless keeps a sync folder on each device in two-way sync with the service copy.

C-02. A file is identified by its path within the sync folder; paths are relative and use forward slashes.

C-03. Every committed change to a file creates a new immutable version.

C-04. The service copy of a file is the version most recently committed for its path.

C-05. Two devices sync only through the service; there are no device-to-device transfers.

C-06. Each device maintains an index of the paths, mtimes, and version ids it last confirmed.

C-07. All client-server communication is over TLS.

C-08. The service is eventually consistent: a change committed on one device is visible to other devices within one sync cycle.

## B. Sync cycle

C-09. A sync cycle runs when a local file event occurs, or 60 seconds after the last cycle, whichever comes first.

C-10. Local file events are debounced: events arriving within 5 seconds of a pending cycle are folded into it.

C-11. In a sync cycle the client uploads local changes, then downloads remote changes.

C-12. A change is committed when the service acknowledges the upload of the complete file.

C-13. Uploads are content-addressed; unchanged content is never re-uploaded.

C-14. A cycle ends with the client and service agreeing on a common version vector for all changed paths.

## C. Conflicts

C-15. A conflict occurs when two devices modify the same path between sync cycles.

C-16. Concurrent modification is resolved newest-wins, comparing client modification timestamps (mtime).

C-17. If both conflicting mtimes are equal, the service copy wins.

C-18. The losing version in a conflict remains recoverable from version history.

C-19. Driftless never attempts to merge file contents; conflict resolution operates on whole files only.

C-20. Conflict resolution is deterministic: the same inputs always select the same winner.

## D. Deletions and tombstones

C-21. A local deletion is recorded as a tombstone and propagated like any other change.

C-22. A tombstone records the path, the deletion timestamp, and the version id that was deleted.

C-23. Tombstones are purged from the deletion log 30 days after the deletion.

C-24. A file can be restored from the deletion log at any time before its tombstone is purged.

C-25. Recreating a file at a deleted path starts a fresh version history; the old history is unaffected.

C-26. Deleting a non-empty folder deletes all contained files and produces one tombstone per file.

## E. Limits

C-27. The maximum size of a single file is 50 GB; larger files are rejected and the rejection is surfaced in sync status.

C-28. File names are at most 255 bytes when encoded as UTF-8.

C-29. Names reserved by Windows (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, and COM1-9, LPT1-9) are rejected on Windows-compatible shares.

C-30. Trailing dots and spaces in file names are stripped before upload.

C-31. Files are transferred in 4 MiB chunks.

C-32. A client uploads at most 4 chunks concurrently.

C-33. Empty files are valid and sync like any other file.

## F. File handling

C-34. Symlinks are skipped: they are neither uploaded nor materialized on other devices.

C-35. Hard links are synced as regular files with no link identity preserved.

C-36. Path handling is case-preserving: the case used at creation is retained.

C-37. A case-insensitive collision (two names differing only in case) causes the newer file to be renamed with a " (1)" suffix before sync.

C-38. Permission bits and ownership are not synced; every platform receives default permissions.

C-39. File locks held by local applications do not block the sync of the last closed state.

## G. Offline and selective sync

C-40. While offline, changes accumulate in a local queue of at most 10000 operations.

C-41. Exceeding the offline queue limit stops the queue from growing; the client requests a full resync on reconnect.

C-42. Selective-sync excluded folders never leave the device; their contents are invisible to the service.

C-43. Pausing sync stops local event capture; resuming runs a full integrity scan before normal cycles continue.

## H. Version history and restore

C-44. Every retained version is addressable by its version id and downloadable.

C-45. Version history for a path is retained for 90 days from the creation of each version.

C-46. Restoring an old version creates a new version with the old content; it never rewrites history.

C-47. Files can be restored from the deletion log for up to 90 days after deletion.

# LedgerPay - Payments API Specification v2.0

This document is the normative contract for the LedgerPay payments HTTP API, version 2.0. Numbered clauses govern; examples are illustrative only.

## A. Overview

C-01. The API base URL is https://api.ledgerpay.example/v2; all paths below are relative to it.

C-02. All requests must be made over TLS; plain HTTP is refused.

C-03. All request and response bodies are JSON encoded as UTF-8.

C-04. Authentication uses a bearer API key in the Authorization header.

C-05. API keys are prefixed test_ in test mode and live_ in production.

C-06. Every response carries an X-Ledgerpay-Request-Id header.

C-07. The API major version appears in the URL path; breaking changes ship only under a new major version.

C-08. Amounts are always integers in minor units (cents) of the stated currency.

## B. Idempotency

C-09. POST requests may carry an Idempotency-Key header.

C-10. Idempotency keys are stored for 24 hours after first use.

C-11. Within the storage window, a repeated request with the same key returns the original response instead of creating a duplicate.

C-12. A repeated request with the same key but a different body is rejected with HTTP 409 and error code idempotency_conflict.

C-13. Idempotency scope is per API key: two keys never share idempotency state.

## C. Money and currencies

C-14. currency is a three-letter ISO 4217 code.

C-15. An unsupported currency is rejected with error code invalid_currency.

C-16. amount must be a positive integer; zero and negative amounts are rejected with error code validation_error.

C-17. Amounts in a currency are never converted by the API; processing occurs in the stated currency.

C-18. Response objects echo amount and currency exactly as submitted.

## D. Authorizations and captures

C-19. POST /authorizations creates an authorization against a payment instrument.

C-20. A successful authorization reserves the authorized amount and returns status authorized.

C-21. An authorization remains capturable for 7 days; after that it expires automatically with status expired.

C-22. POST /authorizations/{id}/capture transfers funds; the captured amount may be less than or equal to the authorized amount.

C-23. Captures may be partial and multiple, provided total captures never exceed the authorized amount.

C-24. Exceeding the authorized amount in captures is rejected with error code capture_limit_exceeded.

C-25. Capturing an expired authorization fails with error code authorization_expired.

C-26. Captured funds are not cancellable; reversal after capture is handled by the refund flow only.

## E. Refunds

C-27. POST /refunds returns funds to the payer against a capture.

C-28. A refund may be partial; total refunds against one capture may not exceed the captured amount.

C-29. Refunds are accepted within 180 days of the capture.

C-30. A refund against a capture older than 180 days is rejected with error code refund_window_closed.

C-31. Refund status lifecycle is pending, settled, or failed.

## F. Webhooks

C-32. Webhooks are delivered by HTTPS POST to registered endpoints only.

C-33. Every webhook carries a Ledgerpay-Signature header computed as HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body with the endpoint secret.

C-34. Receivers should verify the signature before trusting a webhook body.

C-35. A webhook that is not acknowledged with a 2xx response is retried with exponential backoff.

C-36. Webhook retries continue for 24 hours, after which delivery is abandoned.

C-37. Webhook delivery order is not guaranteed; receivers must order events by the event timestamp.

## G. Transport and rate limits

C-38. TLS versions below 1.2 are refused at handshake.

C-39. The rate limit is 100 requests per second per API key, with a burst allowance of 200 requests.

C-40. Exceeding the rate limit returns HTTP 429 with error code rate_limited and a Retry-After header.

C-41. Rate limits are enforced per API key, not per IP address.

C-42. Requests must set a User-Agent header; missing User-Agent is rejected with HTTP 400.

## H. Errors and disputes

C-43. Error responses carry code, message, and request_id.

C-44. Common card errors include card_declined, insufficient_funds, and expired_card.

C-45. A declined authorization is final; the same request must not be retried unchanged within the same hour.

C-46. Cardholders may open a dispute against a capture; the merchant must respond within 10 days.

C-47. An unanswered dispute is decided automatically against the merchant when the 10-day window closes.

## I. Operations and test mode

C-48. Test mode mirrors production behavior with simulated instruments; no real funds move.

C-49. The test card number 4242424242424242 always authorizes successfully.

C-50. Idempotency keys are retained for 72 hours after first use, giving nightly batch jobs a generous replay window.

C-51. Production incidents are communicated on the status page; the API status endpoint reflects component health.

# AuthGate - Access Service Configuration and Behavior v1.1

This document specifies token lifetimes, session behavior, and credential policy for the AuthGate access service, version 1.1. Numbered clauses are normative.

## A. Overview

C-01. AuthGate issues and validates access credentials for the platform's service APIs.

C-02. Credentials come in two kinds: short-lived access tokens and long-lived refresh tokens.

C-03. The service exposes login, refresh, and logout endpoints; all are HTTPS-only.

C-04. All configuration in this document applies per environment (staging and production run the same policy values).

C-05. Times and expirations are computed in UTC.

C-06. This document covers interactive human logins only; machine-to-machine credentials are out of scope.

## B. Access tokens

C-07. Access tokens are JSON Web Tokens signed with RS256.

C-08. The token header carries a kid identifying the signing key.

C-09. An access token is valid for 15 minutes after issuance.

C-10. The token body carries sub (user id), role, and exp claims.

C-11. Validators must reject tokens whose exp is in the past, allowing a clock skew of 60 seconds.

C-12. Validators must reject tokens signed with an unknown kid.

C-13. Access tokens are presented as a bearer token in the Authorization header.

## C. Refresh tokens and sessions

C-14. A refresh token is issued together with the access token at login.

C-15. Refresh tokens are valid for 30 days from issuance.

C-16. Every use of a refresh token rotates it: the old token is invalidated and a new one is issued.

C-17. Presentation of a refresh token that was already rotated revokes the whole session.

C-18. A user may hold at most 5 concurrent sessions; a sixth login revokes the oldest session.

C-19. A session terminates after 8 hours of inactivity (idle timeout).

C-20. Regardless of activity, a session ends 12 hours after it started (absolute lifetime).

C-21. Logout invalidates the current session and both of its tokens.

## D. Passwords and lockout

C-22. Passwords must be at least 12 characters long.

C-23. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt at cost 12; plaintext is never stored or logged.

C-24. Five consecutive failed logins lock the account for 15 minutes.

C-25. A successful login resets the consecutive-failure counter.

C-26. Login attempts are rate-limited to 10 per minute per source IP.

C-27. Password changes invalidate all other sessions of that user.

## E. OTP and MFA

C-28. One-time codes are 6 digits, valid for 5 minutes.

C-29. An OTP attempt counter allows at most 3 tries per code.

C-30. Exceeding the OTP attempt limit invalidates the code and requires a new one.

C-31. Members may opt in to MFA; it is optional for the member role.

C-32. Users with the admin role must have MFA enrolled; login without MFA is refused for admins.

## F. Keys and rotation

C-33. Signing keys rotate every 90 days.

C-34. During a 7-day grace period after rotation, tokens signed with the previous key remain valid.

C-35. Key rotation never shortens the validity of tokens issued before the rotation.

C-36. The public keys for all valid kids are published at the JWKS endpoint.

## G. Platform and audit policy

C-37. Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Lax attributes.

C-38. Every login, logout, refresh, and lockout event is written to the audit log.

C-39. Audit log entries are retained for 400 days.

C-40. Access tokens issued by this service remain valid for 30 minutes after issuance, giving client integrations a generous validation window.

"""Cart totals for the storefront."""

BULK_THRESHOLD = 10
BULK_DISCOUNT = 0.9  # 10 percent off bulk orders


def total_price(unit_price, quantity):
    """Total price in dollars for quantity units of one product.

    The bulk discount applies to orders of BULK_THRESHOLD units or more.
    """
    subtotal = unit_price * quantity
    if quantity < BULK_THRESHOLD:
        subtotal *= BULK_DISCOUNT
    return round(subtotal, 2)
